# Iris

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Phase I: Exploratory analysis and diagnostics

```{r part1}
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)

# Download the UCI Iris data on the first run
dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
iris_file <- "data/iris.data"
if (!file.exists(iris_file)) {
  download.file("https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/iris/iris.data",
                destfile = iris_file)
}

data <- read.csv(iris_file, header = FALSE)
data <- data[data$V5 != "", ]  # drop the empty trailing line, if any
colnames(data) <- c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width", "Species")
summary(data)


# Q-Q plots per species, three side by side
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
for (sp in unique(data$Species)) {
  sub_data <- data[data$Species == sp, "Petal.Length"]
  qqnorm(sub_data, main = paste("Q-Q", sp))
  qqline(sub_data, col = "red")
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
for (sp in unique(data$Species)) {
  sub_data <- data[data$Species == sp, "Sepal.Length"]
  qqnorm(sub_data, main = paste("Q-Q", sp))
  qqline(sub_data, col = "red")
}

for (sp in unique(data$Species)) {
  sub_data <- data[data$Species == sp, "Petal.Width"]
  qqnorm(sub_data, main = paste("Q-Q", sp))
  qqline(sub_data, col = "red")
}

for (sp in unique(data$Species)) {
  sub_data <- data[data$Species == sp, "Sepal.Width"]
  qqnorm(sub_data, main = paste("Q-Q", sp))
  qqline(sub_data, col = "red")
}


# Shapiro-Wilk test for each species separately
tapply(data$Petal.Length, data$Species, shapiro.test)

tapply(data$Petal.Width, data$Species, shapiro.test)

tapply(data$Sepal.Length, data$Species, shapiro.test)

tapply(data$Sepal.Width, data$Species, shapiro.test)

# Box plots
species_colours <- c("Iris-setosa" = "lightpink",
                     "Iris-versicolor" = "lightblue",
                     "Iris-virginica" = "lightyellow")

ggplot(data, aes(x = Species, y = Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Petal length by species", y = "Length (cm)")

ggplot(data, aes(x = Species, y = Petal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Petal width by species", y = "Width (cm)")

ggplot(data, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Sepal length by species", y = "Length (cm)")

ggplot(data, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Sepal width by species", y = "Width (cm)")


# Correlation and scatter plot matrix
ggpairs(data, columns = 1:4, aes(color = Species, alpha = 0.5)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Correlation and scatter plot matrix")


# Covariance matrix of each species (columns 1:4 are the numeric ones, excluding "Species")
cov_matrices <- lapply(split(data[, 1:4], data$Species), cov)
print(cov_matrices)

```

## Phase II: Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA)

```{r part2}
library(MASS)

lda_model <- lda(Species ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width + Petal.Length + Petal.Width,
                 data = data)

# Coefficients and proportion of trace
print(lda_model)

predictions <- predict(lda_model)

```

## Phase III: Evaluation and cross-validation

```{r part3}
set.seed(123)

# Method 1: 70% train / 30% test split
train_idx <- sample(1:nrow(data), size = 0.7 * nrow(data))
train <- data[train_idx, ]
test <- data[-train_idx, ]

# Fit LDA on the training data only
lda_train <- lda(Species ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width + Petal.Length + Petal.Width,
                 data = train)

# Evaluate on the test data
test_predictions <- predict(lda_train, newdata = test)
test_confusion <- table(Actual = test$Species, Predicted = test_predictions$class)
print(test_confusion)


# Method 2: leave-one-out cross-validation (lda with CV = TRUE)
lda_cv <- lda(Species ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width + Petal.Length + Petal.Width,
              data = data, CV = TRUE)

cv_confusion <- table(Actual = data$Species, Predicted = lda_cv$class)
print(cv_confusion)

cv_error <- mean(data$Species != lda_cv$class)
print(paste("Estimated error rate:", round(cv_error * 100, 2), "%"))

cv_accuracy <- sum(diag(cv_confusion)) / sum(cv_confusion)
print(paste("Cross-validated accuracy:", round(cv_accuracy * 100, 2), "%"))
```

## Phase IV: Outliers and robustness

```{r part4}
# Indices of the values outside the 1.5 x IQR fences
find_outliers <- function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75)
  IQR_val <- Q3 - Q1

  lower <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_val
  upper <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_val

  return(which(x < lower | x > upper))
}

outlier_idx <- unique(c(
  find_outliers(data$Sepal.Length),
  find_outliers(data$Sepal.Width),
  find_outliers(data$Petal.Length),
  find_outliers(data$Petal.Width)
))

data_clean <- data[-outlier_idx, ]

print(paste("Observations removed:", length(outlier_idx)))
print(paste("New sample size:", nrow(data_clean)))


# Leave-one-out without the outliers
lda_cv_clean <- lda(Species ~ Sepal.Length + Sepal.Width + Petal.Length + Petal.Width,
                    data = data_clean, CV = TRUE)

cv_confusion_clean <- table(Actual = data_clean$Species, Predicted = lda_cv_clean$class)
print(cv_confusion_clean)

accuracy_clean <- sum(diag(cv_confusion_clean)) / sum(cv_confusion_clean)
print(paste("Cross-validated accuracy (without outliers):", round(accuracy_clean * 100, 2), "%"))
```
